paragraphs.text: My full legal name is Arjun Sharma. I'm married, and my primary residence is in Texas — I live at 123 Main Street, Austin. A few quick answers: no child with special needs, no prior marriages or children outside my current marriage, no real estate outside Texas, no business interests, and I don't expect any family conflicts. Yes, I want a durable financial power of attorney, and yes, I want an advance healthcare directive.
Yes — we have three minor children: Aarav Sharma, age 12, Diya Sharma, age 9, and Kabir Sharma, age 6.

We own our home, worth about $750,000, and we have bank accounts, brokerage and investment accounts, retirement accounts, and life insurance — about $500,000 in savings and investments. Yes, I have retirement accounts, and yes, I have life insurance. Yes, we have significant debts — a mortgage of about $400,000. The beneficiaries on my retirement accounts and life insurance are current: Priya Sharma is the primary beneficiary and our children are the contingent beneficiaries.
No, I don't have any specific bequests. Everything else — the residuary of my estate — goes to my wife Priya Sharma, and if she can't take it, equally to our three children.
My brother Amit Sharma should be the guardian for our children — he is trusted, he is close to the children, and he shares our values. If he can't serve, Neha Kapoor is the backup guardian.
My wife Priya Sharma should be the executor of my will. If she can't serve, my brother Amit Sharma is the backup executor.

A few remaining details: no additional powers beyond the standard ones for my financial agent. My healthcare agent's phone number is 512-555-0100, and there are no limitations on what she may decide. For my living will: if I am terminally ill or permanently unconscious, withhold life-sustaining treatment and keep me on comfort care only. Yes, I wish to donate organs for transplantation.

Yes, I want a revocable living trust. Amit Sharma is the successor trustee. Put everything — all assets — into the trust. The children should receive their inheritance outright at age 25. Everything should go to my spouse outright as the marital share.
